verdict: Uber's operating profit more than doubled to $796M as revenue rose 16% to $10.7B on 2.8 billion trips — and a $333M paper gain on its equity investments helped lift net income to $1.0B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.18 a year ago — flattered by the investment gain below

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 23% to $20.6B.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers. Gross Bookings rose 16% to $18.1B.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue was flat as freight markets stayed soft.

opex.note: Promotions, advertising and winning riders, eaters and drivers.

opex.note: Building the platform and its autonomous-vehicle partnerships.

opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and the back office.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $420M — including a $333M pre-tax gain from revaluing Uber's equity investments — less $139M of interest expense and a $12M loss from equity method investments.
follow100Note: Of the $9.42 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $9.49 accrued to Uber shareholders and non-controlling partners absorbed a $0.07 loss. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income of $1,008M is the total including non-controlling interests; $1,015M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.47 EPS figure) because non-controlling partners absorbed a $7M loss.

takeaways.title: Operating profit more than doubled
takeaways.text: Income from operations jumped 144% to $796M, from $326M a year ago, as revenue growth outpaced costs. Adjusted EBITDA rose 71% to $1,570M.

takeaways.title: Bookings kept growing
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings rose 19% to $40.0B on 2.8 billion trips (+21%). Mobility revenue jumped 25% to $6,134M and Delivery 8% to $3,293M; Freight was flat at $1,273M in a soft trucking market.

takeaways.title: A paper gain padded the bottom line
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Uber was $1,015M, but $333M of it (pre-tax) was an unrealized gain from marking up the value of Uber's equity investments — not cash from rides or deliveries. Free cash flow was $1,721M, up 51%.

oneTimers: Net income includes a $333M pre-tax benefit from net unrealized gains on the revaluation of Uber's equity investments — a paper gain that could reverse if those stocks fall.
